note.p: The entries for Plunket have a pattern which suggests someone close to Ireland. However, it seems unlikely that they refer to William Conyngham Plunket, first Baron Plunket (1764–1854), lord chancellor of Ireland (DNB). The first entries are to Mrs Plunket, whom Godwin meets in Ireland in 1800, and back in London shortly after. There is a link to Curran and Hamilton Rowan. Entries to Plunket in 1804 have a strong link to Hamilton Rowan, but the DNB suggests that even before this time William Conyngham Plunket was embarrassed by his former radicalism, which would make association with Rowan and Godwin odd. Most of the 1807 connections involve King. There is also a Major Plunket in 1807 at Rowans.

Because of the uncertainties around the identification of Plunket, all instances have been coded. However entries for Mrs Plunket sole have been coded as Elizabeth Gunning - see that entry. There are occasions on which he is dining at Plunket's but also mentions Mrs Plunket . Although initially concerned that Mrs Plunket was part of another family (or another generation) we think this indicates his earlier acquaintance with her. rather than the wife of Plunket. The Plural Plunkets have not been coded for Gunning although it is probably she was present.
Godwin also mentions a 'Plunket' in the 1796 list under 1804.
